bestWorstSectors.caption: FMCG surged 1.87% as heavy buying in ITC (+3.54%) and Tata Consumer Products (+3.57%) propelled defensive consumer staples.
Banking stocks gained 0.85% supported by institutional buying in major private and public lenders.
Metal stocks dropped 1.50% as global commodity softness weighed on Tata Steel (-2.81%) and Hindalco.

paragraphs.heading: 1. Monday Session Recap: Nifty climbs 147 points to 25,291; FIIs buy ₹5,737 Cr
paragraphs.body: Indian benchmark indices staged a robust recovery on Monday, 16 November, as the Nifty 50 rose 146.80 points (+0.58%) to close at 25,291.10 and the Sensex surged 510.40 points (+0.63%) to 82,102.85. Buying was heavily concentrated in large-cap heavyweights, banking, and FMCG stocks, while midcaps and smallcaps faced mild profit-taking. Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) remained strong net buyers, injecting a net ₹5,736.55 crore into cash equities.

paragraphs.heading: 2. Overnight Macro Developments (Yesterday 9 AM – Today 7 AM IST): US markets rally & Brent crude eases
paragraphs.body: Overnight global markets provided strong tailwinds. Wall Street indices closed higher (Nasdaq +0.45%, S&P 500 +0.24%) as sentiment stabilized. Crucially, Brent crude oil softened toward $95.00 per barrel (-2.71%) on global supply surplus reports, while the Indian Rupee strengthened to ₹93.95 per US dollar.

paragraphs.heading: 3. Sectors & Industries in Focus Today: Banking, FMCG, Oil-Sensitives, and Metal Laggards
paragraphs.body: As trading opens today, Banking and FMCG stocks remain in focus following their strong momentum. Meanwhile, falling crude oil prices create a positive backdrop for Airlines, Paint Makers, and Oil Marketing Companies, while metal and realty stocks are watched for signs of stabilization.
